counterfactual_missing_items: physical examination was normal, without abdominal wall deficiency
no cryptorchidism or other Prune Belly triad findings are described
no directly visualized posterior urethral valve is reported
decisive_items: bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention
response.rationale: C1 is the strongest composite: it retains the PUV mechanism supported by the dilated bladder and bladder wall thickening/ureteric dilation, and it additionally captures the explicit complication Oligohydramnios. R2 is the same base diagnosis but lacks that complication. R1 is less likely because Prune Belly Syndrome would require abdominal wall deficiency; the normal physical examination and obstructive bladder findings favor Posterior Urethral Mid-instantly.

rejected.why: Prune Belly Syndrome shares nonspecific obstructive uropathy features, but the vignette notes a normal physical exam and no abdominal wall insufficiency or cryptorchidism, while the bladder wall thickening and urinary retention support posterior urethral obstruction.
